summary: Snohomish County 35-ft L-4 pole lookout, built 1934 or 1935, abandoned 1959; WWII aircraft-warning post 1942-43; tower gone, ruins reported.

facts.design: 35-foot wooden pole tower with L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Removal date unknown; one account says it was knocked down or fell down before 1970 and ruins remain; a WillhiteWeb visit describes tower poles and footings in the brush
facts.agency: Washington State Schools (administrator per the Former Fire Lookout Sites register)

access.note: Road gated and blocked with timbers about 200 feet up; about a mile of walking on decommissioned logging roads; decommissioned until the next timber harvest

visit.trail_note: About a 1-mile walk on decommissioned logging roads past the gate; no standing tower to climb

events.note: Built as a 35-foot pole tower with L-4 cab; photos dated July 15, 1935 exist; the register and Firelookout.com give 1934
Activated as Aircraft Warning Service Station 'Yoke 5-3' on July 29, 1942; sleeping quarters 10 x 12 added using AWS resources
AWS station inactivated July 1, 1943; Forest Service retained the site as a fire detection point
Registered October 30, 2010; nominated by Irene Potter

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and Firelookout.com give 1934; WillhiteWeb, Forest Lookouts and Discover Darrington give 1935, and photos are dated July 15, 1935. The story uses 1935 and flags 1934.
The register names Washington State Schools as administrator; Forest Lookouts says the Forest Service kept the site after the AWS station closed. Both are reported.

Register says the removal date is unclear; Discover Darrington says it was knocked down or fell down before 1970, with ruins remaining; Forest Lookouts lists it as removed. Not resolved; all three are reported.

notes_for_editor: Build year disputed (1934 vs 1935); story uses 1935. Removal date unknown. Today's remains rest on an undated WillhiteWeb visit and a Discover Darrington note; no recent photo. Access 'restricted' is a judgement from the gated road on national forest land. No new photo URLs captured. Staffing as a fire lookout not named in any source.
